headline: Sánchez wins 18th as Phillies down Mets 7-2
recap: The Phillies closed out their series at Citi Field with a 7-2 win over the Mets on Sunday. Philadelphia scored twice in the first: Luis Arraez's sacrifice fly to left, on a tag play the Mets challenged and lost, brought home Kyle Schwarber, and Alec Bohm's single drove in Bryce Harper. The Phillies made it 4-0 in the third when Trea Turner's double scored Schwarber and Luis Arraez's single brought home Turner. Bo Bichette's solo home run in the sixth and Brett Baty's RBI single in the seventh cut the deficit to 4-2, but Justin Crawford's three-run triple in the eighth, scoring Bryson Stott, Brandon Marsh and J.T. Realmuto, put the game away. Cristopher Sánchez earned his 18th win, allowing two runs over 6.1 innings with six strikeouts and no walks; Jonah Tong took the loss for New York.
The win moved the Phillies to 86-70, second in the NL East, 6.0 games behind the first-place Braves, and snapped a two-game losing streak.

The Phillies are off Monday before opening a three-game series at home against the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday. First pitch at Citizens Bank Park is scheduled for 6:40 PM ET, with Zack Wheeler starting for Philadelphia against Milwaukee right-hander Dustin May. Betting lines for the series opener were not yet available.
